mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1.5%, it predicts positive 20-day forward returns for the S&P 500 as lower rates compress discount rates and boost equity valuations. The signal is always active, so we always predict positive returns, but the prediction is only expected to be accurate when FEDFUNDS <= 1.5%.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS <= 1.5%, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases (t-test p>0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it predicts negative 20-day forward returns for the S&P 500 as high rates signal monetary tightening that reduces equity valuations. The signal activates when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases (t-test p>0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is above 100 and unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4.0%, it predicts positive 60-day forward returns for the S&P 500 as strong supply growth and low unemployment indicate a robust economy. The signal activates when both conditions hold.
failure_condition: When INDPRO > 100 and UNRATE < 4.0, the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases (t-test p>0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by GDP growth above 2.0% and consumer spending above 680000), the S&P 500 predicts negative 60-day forward returns as late-cycle conditions increase recession risk and reduce equity valuations. The signal activates when GDPC1 > 19700 and RSAFS > 680000.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 > 19700 and RSAFS > 680000, the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases (t-test p>0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 4.0%, it predicts negative 20-day forward returns for the S&P 500 as high unemployment signals economic weakness and reduced corporate earnings. The signal activates when UNRATE > 4.0.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 4.0, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases (t-test p>0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) are above 1500, they predict positive 20-day forward returns for the S&P 500 as strong housing activity signals a healthy economy and increased consumer spending. The signal is always active, so we always predict positive returns, but the prediction is only expected to be accurate when HOUST > 1500.
failure_condition: When HOUST > 1500, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases (t-test p>0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 300, it predicts negative 60-day forward returns for the S&P 500 as high inflation erodes purchasing power and increases the risk of aggressive monetary policy. The signal activates when CPIAUCSL > 300.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 300, the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases (t-test p>0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: When the labor force (PAYEMS) exceeds 150000, it predicts positive 20-day forward returns for the S&P 500 as strong employment growth signals economic expansion and increased consumer spending. The signal activates when PAYEMS > 150000.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS > 150000, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases (t-test p>0.05 for positive returns).
